steps.title: Local Postgres harness + migration skeleton (9999_init.sql sections 0–4)
steps.goal: A developer or CI with PostgreSQL 16 and no Docker can run `scripts/db/local-up.sh` (system cluster or `initdb` fallback, Supabase-like shim with `churchapp_owner` NOSUPERUSER BYPASSRLS, `auth`/`storage`/`extensions`), then `scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh` twice and `scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh`, and get `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` sections (0)–(4) applied: owner-bypassrls assertion, extensions/schemas/default-privilege revokes, all 21 guarded enums, all 38 public + 3 private tables with checks and indexes (including the new `organization_settings.sermon_share_allow_download` and the one-head-per-household partial unique index), `app.touch_updated_at` and `app.assert_same_org` with their triggers, and the drop-all-`ca_%`-policies-and-views block. A stub `scripts/db/test.sh` makes the standing verification sequence runnable from this step on.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 1.2 "Local Postgres harness + migration skeleton (9999_init.sql sections 0–4)" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §4 (all of it, especially "Tables", "Enums" and "Migration skeleton") and §12 "DB", and `docs/DESIGN.md` §4.1, §4.2, §4.4 sections (0)–(4), §12 (local DB, re-runnability guard) and §13 risks 1–3 before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a developer (or CI) with PostgreSQL 16 installed and no Docker can bring up a local database, apply `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` twice in a row without error, and have every enum, all 38 public tables and 3 private tables, their checks and indexes, the `touch_updated_at` and `assert_same_org` trigger functions with their triggers, and the "drop all `ca_%` policies and our views" block in place. `scripts/db/local-up.sh`, `scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh`, `scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh` and a minimal `scripts/db/test.sh` exist and work; `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` makes the local cluster look enough like Supabase (roles, `auth`, `storage`, `extensions`) for the migration and for the RLS tests of step 1.4. No helper functions beyond the two trigger functions, no views, no RPCs, no policies, no grants, no storage buckets yet — those are steps 1.3a, 1.3b and 1.4. The founder can already read the top of `9999_init.sql` and see the whole data model.

## Inputs / prior state
- Step 1.1 produced the pnpm/turbo workspace; the root `package.json` already declares `db:up`, `db:apply`, `db:test`, `db:check` and `db:types` scripts pointing at `scripts/db/*.sh` (they fail today because the files do not exist — this step creates all but `gen-types.sh`, which is step 1.5). `docs/ENV.md` documents `DATABASE_URL`; `.gitignore` already ignores `.local-pg/` and `supabase/.temp/`.
- Nothing exists under `supabase/` or `scripts/db/`. Do not create `supabase/seed/`, `supabase/tests/helpers.sql`, `supabase/tests/rls/*` or `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` (steps 1.4 and 1.5).
- Machine facts (PLAN "Environment facts", DESIGN §12): PostgreSQL 16.13 is installed, cluster `main` may be down, Docker is down, `npx supabase` 2.116 exists but `supabase start` is impossible. `initdb` refuses to run as root, so the fallback path must run as the `postgres` OS user (or the current user when not root).
- Founder decisions that touch this step: decision 5 adds `organization_settings.sermon_share_allow_download boolean not null default false`; decision 3 keeps the youth/adult age columns exactly as modelled (no schema change); decision 6 keeps `push_on_bulletin` default true; decision 7: "trial 30 days (`trial_ends_at` default now()+30d on church creation)" — give the column `default now() + interval '30 days'` (DESIGN §4.2 shows no default; record the addition under "Deviations from plan") so the trial exists even when a church is created by SQL, and keep the extensible `billing_mode` enum (step 2.2 may still display or override the date); decision 10 (Supabase Free) affects only the storage section of step 1.4. Orchestrator decision 6: at most one `head` per household, enforced by a partial unique index.
- Orchestrator decisions 15 and 21 (2026-09-07/08): `9999_init.sql` is not pasted anywhere yet, so the schema corrections found while drafting later steps live HERE, not in a later migration. They are: the account-archival columns on `profiles` and `account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for` (decision 15 — the self-service action is Deactivate, which archives; real deletion stays because Google Play requires it, with a 30-day grace, `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30`), `organizations.cancelled_at` (drives the 30-day purge in `srv_housekeeping`), `bulletins.publish_at` / `documents.publish_at` explicitly nullable (null = draft, so uploads follow the insert-then-publish flow), `documents.description`, `calendars.members_can_submit` (leaders-only calendars), and the FK actions on `announcements.document_id` / `audience_group_id` (`on delete set null`). Each is marked in the table list below; steps 1.3a/1.3b add the matching triggers and RPCs.

## Build
1. `supabase/config.toml`: the minimal file `npx supabase init` would generate (`project_id = "churchappcld"`, `[db] major_version = 16`, `[api] schemas = ["public"]`), with a header comment: "used only by `supabase gen types --db-url` and a future `supabase start`; NEVER run `supabase db push` or `supabase db reset` against this project — migrations are pasted by hand (docs/PLAN.md §4)". Do not run `npx supabase init`; write the file.
2. `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` — local-only, applied by `local-up.sh` as the cluster superuser, idempotent (every statement `if not exists` / `create or replace` / `do $$ … $$` guarded), and clearly headed "NOT a migration; never paste into Supabase". It creates:
   - Roles `anon` and `authenticated` as `nologin`; `service_role` as `nologin bypassrls` (Supabase's service role bypasses RLS — the service client in the cron and in Server Actions relies on it to write `notifications`, `storage_deletions`, `stripe_events` and `billing_*` rows, which have no `authenticated` write policies); guard each `create role` with `if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = …)`. `churchapp_owner` as `login nosuperuser nocreaterole bypassrls` with the dev-only password `churchapp` (needed only when the system cluster's `pg_hba.conf` demands a password over TCP): guard the `create role` the same way, then run `alter role churchapp_owner login nosuperuser nocreaterole bypassrls password 'churchapp'` UNCONDITIONALLY so the attributes converge even when `local-up.sh` pre-created the role (see 3.4) or an older shim left it different; likewise `alter role service_role bypassrls` unconditionally. Grant `anon`, `authenticated`, `service_role` to `churchapp_owner` so tests can `set role`. This mirrors Supabase's `postgres` role: NOT a superuser, but BYPASSRLS (DESIGN §1 item 1 — "the local shim uses a non-superuser bypassrls owner so parity is real").
   - Schemas `extensions`, `auth`, `storage` (owner `churchapp_owner`); `grant usage on schema extensions, auth, storage to anon, authenticated, service_role`; `alter database churchapp set search_path` is NOT touched.
   - `auth.users` with the columns the migration and tests need: `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()`, `email text unique`, `raw_user_meta_data jsonb not null default '{}'`, `raw_app_meta_data jsonb not null default '{}'`, `created_at timestamptz default now()`, `updated_at timestamptz default now()`, `deleted_at timestamptz`, `last_sign_in_at timestamptz`, owned by `churchapp_owner` (step 1.3a creates triggers on it, which requires ownership). `auth.uid()` returns `coalesce(nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), ''), nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub')::uuid`; `auth.jwt()` returns `coalesce(nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim', true), ''), nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), ''))::jsonb`; `auth.role()` returns the `role` claim the same way — all three `language sql stable`. Tests in 1.4 will "log in" with `set local role authenticated; select set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', uid, 'role', 'authenticated')::text, true)`.
   - `storage.buckets` (`id text primary key, name text not null unique, owner uuid, public boolean default false, file_size_limit bigint, allowed_mime_types text[], created_at timestamptz default now(), updated_at timestamptz default now()`) and `storage.objects` (`id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(), bucket_id text references storage.buckets(id), name text, owner uuid, owner_id text, metadata jsonb, path_tokens text[] generated always as (string_to_array(name, '/')) stored, version text, created_at, updated_at, last_accessed_at timestamptz`), both owned by `churchapp_owner` (1.4 creates policies on `storage.objects`); functions `storage.foldername(name text) returns text[]` (all path segments but the last), `storage.filename(name text) returns text`, `storage.extension(name text) returns text` — `language sql immutable`.
   - Grant `all` on all tables in `auth`/`storage` to `churchapp_owner`; grant `select` on `storage.buckets` and `storage.objects` to `anon`, and `select, insert, update, delete` on `storage.objects` and `storage.buckets` to `authenticated`, `service_role` (Supabase grants these table privileges; the `ca_storage_*` policies of step 1.4 do the filtering). `alter table storage.objects enable row level security` (guard with `pg_class.relrowsecurity`; RLS is on for `storage.objects` on Supabase, so without it a 1.4 test would see writes the hosted database blocks). Never `force row level security`.
   - A trailing `do $$ … raise notice 'shim applied' $$`. Note in the header that `local-up.sh` re-applies the shim on EVERY run (it is idempotent), so a later tweak reaches an existing local database without dropping it; the only database that never sees the shim is one reached through the `DATABASE_URL` short-circuit in 3.2 (a hosted-style database that already has `auth.uid()`).
3. `scripts/db/local-up.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, executable, every path quoted). Behaviour, in order:
   1. Resolve `REPO_ROOT` from the script location; `STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.local-pg"` (gitignored).
   2. If `DATABASE_URL` is already set and `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c 'select 1'` succeeds, print it and exit 0 (a hosted-style database that is already prepared — no shim, no role creation).
   3. Decide the superuser access MODE, then define ONE helper used for every superuser statement in every path: `super_sql() { case "$MODE" in url) psql "$PG_SUPER_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; cluster) sudo -u postgres psql -p "$PORT" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; initdb) psql "postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PORT/postgres" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; esac; }` (when already running as root use `su postgres -c` / `runuser -u postgres --` instead of `sudo`, whichever exists). Feed SQL FILES to it on stdin, never by path — `super_sql -f - < "$REPO_ROOT/supabase/tests/00_shim.sql"` — because in `cluster` mode the `postgres` OS user usually cannot read files inside the repo (a `700` home or `/root`). The modes, tried in order:
      - **Path 0 (`MODE=url`)** — when `PG_SUPER_URL` is set (CI's `postgres:16` service container, or a Docker / `npx supabase start` database on the founder's machine at `postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres`, DESIGN §12): use it for every superuser statement, skip Paths A and B, and derive `DATABASE_URL` by replacing user, password and database in `PG_SUPER_URL` with `churchapp_owner`, `churchapp`, `churchapp` (keep host, port and query string).
      - **Path A (`MODE=cluster`)**: `pg_ctlcluster 16 main start` (as `postgres` when root; treat "already running" as success). Superuser access is `sudo -u postgres psql` (peer auth); port from `pg_lsclusters`.
      - **Path B (`MODE=initdb`, when A fails — no cluster, no permission)**: `initdb` refuses to run as root, so when root run `initdb`/`pg_ctl` as the `postgres` OS user, otherwise as the current user. Before `initdb`: `mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"`; when root, `chown postgres "$STATE_DIR"`; if `sudo -u postgres test -w "$STATE_DIR"` still fails (untraversable parent directories such as `/root`), use `PGDATA_DIR="${LOCAL_PG_DATA:-/var/lib/postgresql/churchapp-local}"` instead of `$STATE_DIR/pg` and record the path in `$STATE_DIR/PGDATA` (the URL files always stay in `.local-pg/`). Then `initdb -D "$PGDATA_DIR" -A trust -U postgres --no-locale -E UTF8` (skip when the directory exists), pick the first free port from 5433 upward (loop with `pg_isready`/`ss -ltn`), then `pg_ctl -D "$PGDATA_DIR" -o "-p $PORT -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1 -k $STATE_DIR" -l "$STATE_DIR/pg.log" start` (skip when already running per `pg_ctl status`). Superuser URL is `postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PORT/postgres`.
   4. Create the owner role BEFORE the database, with its FULL attributes, in one guarded statement through `super_sql`: `do $$ begin if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'churchapp_owner') then create role churchapp_owner login nosuperuser nocreaterole bypassrls password 'churchapp'; end if; end $$;` — the shim's own `churchapp_owner` block then runs `alter role …` unconditionally (Build 2), so the attributes converge whichever ran first.
   5. Create the database if missing — `createdb` has no connection parameters for a URL-based superuser, so use the helper: `super_sql -tAc "select 1 from pg_database where datname = 'churchapp'" | grep -q 1 || super_sql -c "create database churchapp owner churchapp_owner"`. Owning the database gives `churchapp_owner` the CREATE privilege that trusted extensions (`pgcrypto`, `citext`) require in PG16. Then apply the full shim against `churchapp` on EVERY run (it is idempotent): `super_sql -d churchapp -f - < "$REPO_ROOT/supabase/tests/00_shim.sql"` (in `url` mode swap the database name inside the URL instead of passing `-d`).
   6. Compute `DATABASE_URL`: Path 0 → derived from `PG_SUPER_URL` as above; Path B → `postgresql://churchapp_owner@127.0.0.1:$PORT/churchapp?sslmode=disable`; Path A → `postgresql://churchapp_owner:churchapp@127.0.0.1:$PORT/churchapp?sslmode=disable` (Debian's default `pg_hba.conf` uses scram over TCP, hence the dev password; document this in `docs/ENV.md` next to the existing `DATABASE_URL` row). Write `$STATE_DIR/DATABASE_URL` always. Write `$STATE_DIR/PG_SUPER_URL` only in Paths 0 and B (where a URL works); in Path A write `$STATE_DIR/SUPER_PSQL` containing `sudo -u postgres psql -p <port>` instead, because peer auth has no URL the current user can use. Print `export DATABASE_URL=…` as the last line (mask any password). Verify with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select current_user || ' ' || current_setting('server_version')"` → `churchapp_owner 16.x`.
   7. Add `scripts/db/_env.sh` (sourced by the other scripts): sets `REPO_ROOT`, and `DATABASE_URL` from the environment or `$REPO_ROOT/.local-pg/DATABASE_URL`, failing with "run scripts/db/local-up.sh first" when neither exists; exposes a `super_psql "$@"` function — `psql "$PG_SUPER_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@"` when `PG_SUPER_URL` is in the environment or in `.local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL`, else the command stored in `.local-pg/SUPER_PSQL` — so later scripts (1.4a's database reset, 1.5's seed) run superuser statements regardless of path.
4. `scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh`: sources `_env.sh`; lists `supabase/migrations/*.sql`; sorts by the 4-digit numeric prefix DESCENDING (9999 first — highest number = oldest = applied first) and, within one number, by the letter suffix ASCENDING (`9998a_enum.sql` before `9998b_use.sql`); applies each with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f "$file"` and prints `applied <file>`; exits non-zero on the first failure. `--single-transaction` matches the SQL editor (one paste = one transaction) and is why enum value additions must live in their own file. Optional `--only <file>` argument for debugging. Print the final line `applied N migration(s) to $DATABASE_URL` (mask the password).
5. `scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh`: a static checker (bash + `grep -nE`/`awk`, or a small Python 3 script invoked from bash — Python 3 is present) over every `supabase/migrations/*.sql`, implementing exactly the rules of DESIGN §12 "Re-runnability guard" and PLAN §12: fail if (a) any `create policy` is not preceded (anywhere earlier in the file) by `drop policy if exists <same name>`; (b) any `create trigger <name> on <table>` lacks a preceding `drop trigger if exists <name> on <table>`; (c) any `create type` appears outside a `do $$ … if not exists … $$` block (approximate: the `create type` line must be inside a `do $$` block whose text contains `if not exists`); (d) any `create table`/`create index`/`create unique index`/`create schema`/`create extension` lacks `if not exists`; (e) any `create function` is neither `create or replace function` nor preceded by `drop function if exists <name>`; (f) any `create view` lacks a preceding `drop view if exists <name>`; (g) any function definition (from `create or replace function` to the end of its body — the closing `$$` tag or `;`) lacks `security definer` OR lacks `set search_path = ''` — report which clause is missing (DESIGN §12 and PLAN §12 require BOTH on every function); (h) any unqualified `crypt(`, `gen_salt(`, `gen_random_bytes(`, `digest(` (i.e. not preceded by `extensions.`); (i) a file containing `add value` also contains that value as a quoted literal elsewhere; (j) any `create policy` whose name does not start with `ca_`; (k) any `force row level security`. Print `OK <file>` or every violation as `file:line: rule (x): message`; exit 1 on any violation. Make rule (g) tolerant of `language sql`/`language plpgsql` order and of line breaks. Add a `--self-test` flag that runs the checker against a few inline bad snippets written to `$REPO_ROOT/.local-pg/rerun-selftest/` (created and emptied by the script; gitignored with the rest of `.local-pg/`) and asserts each rule fires — for (g) include one snippet missing only `security definer` and one missing only `set search_path` (this is the checker's own test).
6. `scripts/db/test.sh` (minimal; step 1.4 extends it): sources `_env.sh`; if `supabase/tests/helpers.sql` exists, applies it first (`ON_ERROR_STOP=1`); then runs every `supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` in name order with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f`; prints `PASS <file>`/`FAIL <file>`; exits 1 on any failure; when the `rls/` directory is absent or empty prints `no RLS tests yet (step 1.4)` and exits 0. This makes the standing verification sequence runnable from this step on.
7. `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` — sections (0)–(4) of the skeleton in PLAN §4 "Migration skeleton" and DESIGN §4.4. Write the file with a section header comment per section, e.g. `-- ===== (3) tables =====`, and reserve headers for (5)–(11) with a one-line `-- filled in step 1.3a / 1.3b / 1.4` placeholder each so later steps insert in the right place. Content:
   - Header comment: re-runnable; paste into the Supabase SQL editor as many times as needed; frozen after the first production paste (HANDOFF ledger).
   - (0) exactly the owner assertion from DESIGN §4.4 (`rolbypassrls or rolsuper` for `current_user`, else `raise exception`).
   - (1) exactly the extensions/schemas/default-privilege block from DESIGN §4.4: `create extension if not exists pgcrypto with schema extensions`, `citext` likewise, `create schema if not exists app`, `create schema if not exists private`, the four `revoke`/`grant` lines and the four `alter default privileges` lines. Do not create the `extensions` schema in the migration (Supabase owns it; the shim creates it locally).
   - (2) all 21 enums, each in its own `do $$ if not exists … $$` guard (one `do` block per type, so a later `9998a` paste can copy the pattern). Values — copy verbatim where the docs give them, otherwise use these and keep them: `permission_key` (the 12 values in PLAN §4 order); `org_status` (`trial, active, past_due, suspended, cancelled`); `billing_mode` (`stripe, manual, free`); `subscription_status` (`trialing, active, past_due, canceled, unpaid, incomplete, incomplete_expired, paused, none, unknown`); `membership_status` (`pending, active, disabled`); `congregation_status` (`member, attendee, inactive`); `sex` (`male, female`); `marital_status` (`unknown, single, married, widowed, divorced`); `household_role` (`head, spouse, child, other`); `birthdate_visibility` (`full, month_day, hidden`); `media_kind` (`upload, youtube, dropbox, google_drive, url`); `audience_kind` (`everyone, members, attendees, youth, men, women, custom`); `calendar_kind` (`all, youth, men, women, custom`); `event_status` (`pending, approved, rejected, cancelled`); `survey_status` (`draft, open, closed`); `response_mode` (`per_person, per_household`); `question_kind` (`short_text, long_text, single_choice, multi_choice, yes_no, number, date`); `notification_kind` (`announcement, event, survey, bulletin`); `notification_status` (`queued, claimed, sent, failed, cancelled`); `push_platform` (`android, ios`); `join_request_status` (`pending, approved, rejected`).
   - (3) `create table if not exists` for all 38 public tables and 3 private tables, in dependency order, with `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()` (unless the docs give another PK), `created_at`/`updated_at timestamptz not null default now()` on every table that is ever updated, `org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade` + `create index if not exists <table>_org_id_idx` on every tenant table, `extensions.citext` for emails and slugs. Copy the column lists and constraints from DESIGN §4.2 and the SQL in §4.4 verbatim for `organizations` (with two additions: `trial_ends_at timestamptz default now() + interval '30 days'` — founder decision 7 — and `cancelled_at timestamptz` with the comment "set by the `organizations_stamp_org_status` trigger (step 1.3a) when status becomes `cancelled`; drives the 30-day purge in `srv_housekeeping`"), `organization_settings` (ADD `sermon_share_allow_download boolean not null default false` — founder decision 5: "DOWNLOADS ALLOWED when the church allows it → NEW column `organization_settings.sermon_share_allow_download boolean not null default false`"), `households`, `household_leader_notes`, `persons` (+ the partial unique `persons_org_user_unique`, indexes `(org_id, household_id)`, `(org_id, birthdate)`, and the NEW `create unique index if not exists persons_one_head_per_household on public.persons (household_id) where household_role = 'head'` — orchestrator decision 6), `person_leader_notes`, `sermons` (+ `sermons_storage_path_unique`), `billing_subscriptions`. For the tables the docs describe only by key columns use exactly these columns (names chosen here because the docs leave them open; later steps depend on them): `fellowships` (`id, slug citext unique, name, description, created_at, updated_at`); `fellowship_memberships` (`fellowship_id fk cascade, org_id fk cascade, joined_at default now()`, PK `(fellowship_id, org_id)`); `profiles` (`user_id uuid pk references auth.users(id) on delete cascade, display_name text, email citext, last_org_id uuid references organizations on delete set null, archived_at timestamptz, archived_by uuid, archive_reason text check (archive_reason is null or archive_reason in ('user','deletion_request','admin')), created_at, updated_at` — the three `archived_*` columns are orchestrator decision 15: `archived_at is not null` means the account is deactivated and every `app.*` membership helper (1.3a) treats the user as a non-member; `archived_by` null = the user themself; `comment on column` each of them); `super_admins` (`user_id pk fk auth.users cascade, granted_by uuid, created_at`); `org_memberships` (`id, org_id, user_id fk auth.users cascade, status membership_status default 'pending', invited_by, approved_by, approved_at, disabled_at, created_at, updated_at`, `unique (org_id, user_id)`, index `(user_id, status)`); `org_membership_permissions` (`membership_id fk org_memberships cascade, permission permission_key, granted_by uuid, granted_at default now()`, PK `(membership_id, permission)`); `invitations` (`id, org_id, email citext not null, person_id fk persons on delete set null, permissions permission_key[] not null default '{}', invited_by, expires_at default now() + interval '14 days', accepted_at, accepted_by, revoked_at, created_at, updated_at`, index `(org_id, email)`); `private.invitation_secrets` (`invitation_id pk fk invitations cascade, token_hash bytea not null unique`); `join_codes` (`id, org_id, code citext not null unique, label text, auto_approve boolean default false, expires_at, max_uses int, use_count int default 0, revoked_at, created_by, created_at, updated_at`, check `char_length(code) = 8`); `join_requests` (`id, org_id, join_code_id fk join_codes set null, user_id fk auth.users cascade, person_id fk persons set null, status join_request_status default 'pending', message text, reviewed_by, reviewed_at, created_at, updated_at`, partial unique `(org_id, user_id) where status = 'pending'`); `account_deletion_requests` (`user_id pk fk auth.users cascade, requested_at timestamptz not null default now(), scheduled_for timestamptz not null default now() + interval '30 days', processed_at timestamptz` — comment on `scheduled_for`: "ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30 (orchestrator decision 15): the account is archived at request time and `srv_process_account_deletions` deletes it only once `scheduled_for` has passed; the user or a super admin cancels in between"); `sermon_share_links` (DESIGN §4.2 columns + `created_at, updated_at`); `private.share_link_secrets` (`link_id pk fk sermon_share_links cascade, token_hash bytea not null unique, password_hash text`); `announcements` (DESIGN columns; `audience_group_id` and `document_id` both `references … on delete set null` — orchestrator decision 21 fixes these FK actions; `pinned boolean default false`; `push boolean default true`; proposed_additional_steps.title: Hosted-parity dry run of 9999_init.sql on a throwaway Supabase project
proposed_additional_steps.goal: Before the founder pastes `9999_init.sql` into the real project (step 2.4), the file is pasted once into a throwaway Supabase Free project to catch hosted-only differences the local shim cannot reproduce (role privileges of `postgres`, `auth.users` trigger ownership, `storage.objects` policy creation, bucket upsert columns, the `extensions` schema), then the project is deleted.
proposed_additional_steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 1.8 "Hosted-parity dry run of 9999_init.sql" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §4 and `docs/DESIGN.md` §12–§13 (risks 3, 13) before doing anything. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
The founder pastes `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` (and optionally `supabase/tests/rls/*.sql`) into a throwaway Supabase project's SQL editor and reports every error verbatim; you fix the migration so it applies twice both locally and hosted, without changing behaviour, and record the differences between the shim and the hosted database in `supabase/README.md`.

## Inputs / prior state
Steps 1.2–1.5 complete; the local sequence is green. The founder gives you the pasted error messages (never keys or URLs).

## Build
1. For each hosted error, reproduce the cause locally if possible (adjust `00_shim.sql` so the local database is closer to hosted — e.g. ownership of `auth.users`, `storage.objects` privileges) and fix `9999_init.sql` re-runnably.
2. Document in `supabase/README.md` a 'Shim vs hosted' section listing what the shim cannot prove (real Auth, Storage, TUS, JWT claims) and what this dry run verified.

## Constraints
Do not weaken any security rule to make the paste succeed; never `supabase db push`; the throwaway project must be deleted by the founder afterwards (Free plan allows two active projects).

## Verify
Local standing sequence green; the founder confirms the second paste on the throwaway project reports no error and `select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname = 'public'` returns 38 there.

## Finish
Update HANDOFF.md (ledger stays empty — the throwaway paste is not production; note the dry run under Environment status), tick 1.8 in `docs/TODO.md`, write `session_log.md`, commit `fix(db): hosted-parity fixes from Supabase dry run`, push `main`.
